body:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: High GPU queue growth detected for pool `inference-gpu-prod`. Autoscaler not responding to custom metrics (HPA). Pager -> oncall. Runbook: <https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/gpu-autoscale>

maya: oncall here, looking. Confirming alerts: queue length ~98%, token-generator queue backlog growing, spikes in 429s.

liam: seeing same. HPA metrics from prometheus-adapter stale: last heartbeat 12m ago. `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` returns errors.

robin: any recent deploys to inference stack? nothing in last 30m in deploy log.

sara: CS is getting paged, some customers report timeouts. I'll start a brief in-prod blurb once we have scope.

maya: pulling HPA and adapter status now.

maya: (paste) `kubectl describe hpa inference-worker` -> "metrics: custom metrics server unavailable, no data in last 10m". HPA shows desired 3 -> current 3, despite queue backlog.

liam: check prometheus-adapter logs: `kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter --since=20m` -> repeated "504 upstream read timeout" to prometheus:9090 and "failed to convert metric: empty response".

robin: prometheus itself ok? `kubectl -n monitoring get pods` shows `prometheus-0` up. Check its health endpoint.

liam: prometheus health endpoints respond but scrape queue length is elevated. Looks like TSDB compaction is running heavy and blocking query frontends.

sara: customer impact: CS lists 12 enterprise customers with elevated error rates on generation endpoints. I'll mark as "degraded" on status page.

maya: immediate mitigation plan:
1) try restart prometheus-adapter (cheap)
2) if adapter restart doesn't restore metrics, manually scale inference deployment to drain queue
3) adjust HPA config later to avoid single-metric choke

maya: executing `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/prometheus-adapter`

deploy-bot: deploy/restart: prometheus-adapter restarted by maya at 2026-03-15T02:38:15Z :rocket:

liam: restarting adapter didn't immediately pick up metrics. I'm going to increase adapter replicas to 3 temporarily: `kubectl -n monitoring scale deploy/prometheus-adapter --replicas=3`.

liam: also seeing a flood of heartbeat metrics from one canary job that started ~25m ago. That job is spamming per-node metrics and causing prometheus write backlog.

robin: can we pause that canary? which namespace?

liam: it's in `ci-loadtests` namespace, job `canary-throttle-xyz`. I'm stopping it: `kubectl -n ci-loadtests delete job canary-throttle-xyz`.

maya: while adapter ramps, manual scale of worker pool to buy time: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-worker --replicas=40` (was 8).

sara: posted preliminary status: "We are experiencing degraded inference throughput due to autoscaling delays. Engineers are mitigating. No data loss. Customers may see elevated latencies and some 429s."

cs-alert-bot: Notified on-call CS and created ticket #INC-8721 for affected customers.

liam: after canary kill + adapter replicas up, custom metrics started flowing again, HPA now sees queue length metric.

maya: HPA now recommending 32 replicas, but our node pool can't provision that fast due to GPU quota per AZ. We'll watch.

robin: observed KPA throttling events in logs: `Error: PodPending: Insufficient nvidia-gpus`. Node autoscaler hitting scale limits for this pool.

liam: manual nodepool ops in progress: requesting extra nodes from cloud (increasing nodepool size, temp quota request). Running `gcloud beta container node-pools resize --node-pool=gpu-pool --cluster=prod-cluster --num-nodes=20`

deploy-bot: cloud request for nodepool resize issued by liam. Queueing provisioning.

maya: queue drain started after manual scale -> 20% reduction in backlog within 6 minutes. But 99p latency still high for some customers.

sara: CS updated customers with ETA ~30m for full recovery; default messaging: "We are actively scaling capacity and restoring autoscaling metrics."

robin: action items during live mitigation:
- keep prometheus-adapter at 3 replicas for 30m
- add a temporary filter to drop ci-loadtests metrics at scrape relabel
- manual scale worker replicas down when backend healthy

liam: adding relabel config to prometheus to drop `job=canary-throttle-xyz` metrics. Applying as quick patch.

maya: note: we should not rely on manual nodepool increases for long. Need graceful fallback: queue rate limiting and client-side 429 pacing.

sara: contacting two top-tier customers individually via CS to notify of degraded experience.

liam: metrics now look stable; HPA progressively scaled workers up to 28 and queue drain continues. Pending verification of quotas and node readiness.

deploy-bot: alert: nodepool resize completed, 18 new nodes ready.

maya: final check: queue at 8%, error rate back to baseline for most customers, some residual 429s for 10 more minutes.

sara: status page set to "degraded -> recovering" and message updated.

robin: root cause hypothesis: a noisy canary induced heavy TSDB write/compaction, causing adapter timeouts and custom metrics blackout; HPA couldn't see metrics -> no autoscale -> queue grew -> manual mitigation required.

maya: handing off to liam for postmortem and follow-up infra tasks. I'll stay available for context. :white_check_mark:

liam: taking over. Post-incident to-do: 1) add relabel rule to permanently drop CI canary metrics, 2) add circuit breaker to prometheus-adapter queries, 3) add alert for adapter-staleness earlier, 4) run a capacity test for nodepool scale limits.

sara: I'll draft post-incident customer communication and link to postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: service status moved to RECOVERING. Duration ~52m. Incident owner: liam. Postmortem requested at <https://wiki.redwood.ai/incidents/6001234567>. :spiral_note_pad:

maya: thanks team, good mitigation. Closing slack thread in 30m unless follow-ups.
